summary:
Legrand is a French manufacturer of electrical and digital building infrastructure, with more than 300,000 products. It operates in 90 countries, sells in nearly 180, and earns 85% of sales internationally.

Founded in Limoges in 1865 as a porcelain workshop, the company took the Legrand name in 1904 and moved into electrical switches in 1919. After a 1949 factory fire, it focused entirely on electrical equipment, expanding into wiring devices, circuit protection, cable management and emergency lighting.

Legrand listed in Paris in 1970 and grew through international expansion and acquisitions. Major steps included Pial in Brazil (1977), Pass & Seymour in the US (1984), Bticino in Italy (1989), and US cabling and lighting-control companies Ortronics, Wiremold and WattStopper in the 1990s and 2000. In 2003, investors KKR and Wendel took the company private; it returned to public trading in 2006. Later acquisitions strengthened its businesses in data centers, connected homes, lighting, cabling, assisted living and electric-vehicle charging. These included Raritan, Netatmo, Milestone AV, Server Technology, Focal Point, Borri, Ensto Building Systems, Ecotap, USystems and Encelium.

A proposed Schneider Electric takeover in 2001 failed after the European Commission raised competition concerns. Schneider had acquired up to 98.1% of Legrand’s shares, but had to sell them; KKR and Wendel became buyers.

Legrand entered EV charging and energy-efficiency markets in 2010. Its offerings now include connected-home and IoT products, lighting controls, EV chargers, data-center power and cooling systems, and assisted-living technologies. In 2021 it launched Legrand Care, bringing together its assisted-living and healthcare brands. It has eight French production sites near Limoges and opened two Paris-area training centers in 2012.

The 2009 crisis cut revenue 15.6% to €3.6 billion, while operating margin held at 17.6%. In 2010, sales rose 8.7%, operating income 35.5%, and net income 44.3% to €418.3 million; margin reached 20.2%. Results were again at record levels in 2021, especially in data centers, connected products and energy efficiency. In 2022, Legrand reported net income growth of 16.1% for the first nine months and signed France’s EcoWatt charter, pledging to reduce energy use.

Benoît Coquart has been CEO since 2018. Angeles Garcia-Poveda has chaired the board since July 2020. Former CEO François Grappotte led the company from 1983 to 2006 and became honorary chair; Gilles Schnepp was CEO from 2006 to 2018 and chair until 2020. Key competitors include Eaton, Hubbell, Leviton and Lutron.
unsupportedClaims: After the 1949 fire, Legrand focused exclusively on electrical equipment generally and later expanded into wiring devices. The decision was to focus exclusively on wiring devices.
Wiremold was a cabling or lighting-control company.
Legrand returned to public trading in 2006. The points establish that shares were traded by the end of 2006, not that public trading resumed that year.
Legrand completed the Milestone AV acquisition. The points say it began the purchase process.
Legrand entered the electric-vehicle charging and energy-efficiency markets in 2010. The points say it announced plans to enter those markets.
Gilles Schnepp remained chair until 2020. The points say he remained president until 2020.
